title: Po crucible made of ice: cold-copper skull-melt Czochralski silicon
idea: Po: 'the crucible is made of ice.' Extracted: pull 300 mm CZ ingots from a melt held in a water-cooled segmented copper crucible, where induction heating levitates and stirs the melt and a frozen silicon skull is the only wall contact, so no high-purity quartz crucible is consumed and no oxygen dissolves from silica walls; a cusp magnetic field damps convection for radial dopant uniformity.
why: Removes the Spruce Pine (>80%) high-purity-quartz crucible chokepoint for DRAM substrates; low-oxygen wafers also remove oxygen-precipitate leakage sites in the retention tail. Cost is ~2-3x melt power per ingot.

title: Po memory sold by the square meter: DRAM tiles on display glass
idea: Po: 'memory is sold by the square meter like carpet.' Extracted: run oxide-TFT gain-cell arrays on Gen-8.5 (2.2 x 2.5 m) display glass in under-used LCD fabs, then cut the panel into memory tiles mounted beside processors. One panel has ~80x the area of a 300 mm wafer and uses no single-crystal silicon, no quartz crucible and no EUV.
why: Capital intensity and crucible/polysilicon intensity: display-fab cost per cm2 is several times lower than DRAM-wafer cost per cm2, so a low-density capacity tier could still be competitive in bits per capital dollar. It also brings a non-DRAM industry's idle capacity into memory.

title: Po helium is a fab export: closed-loop recapture at every tool
idea: Po: 'the fab exports helium instead of importing it.' Extracted: hood every helium user (ESC backside cooling exhaust, leak checkers, load-lock purge, carrier gas) with point-of-use recovery manifolds feeding a central compressor, a polymer-membrane pre-concentrator and a cryogenic purifier back to 6N, so purchases shrink to make-up for leakage.
why: Helium chokepoint (Qatar ~30% of supply offline since March 2026): 85-95% recovery cuts purchased helium ~10x and makes the fab immune to spot shortages; payback likely under 2 years at 2026 prices.

title: Po the chuck is a hairbrush: gas-free nanofiber thermal contact
idea: Po: 'the wafer is cooled by a hairbrush, not a gas.' Extracted: replace helium backside gas in electrostatic chucks with a dense, vertically aligned boron-nitride-nanotube or carbon-nanotube forest capped with a thin alumina skin, whose millions of compliant tips conduct heat under electrostatic clamping as well as ~10 Torr of helium.
why: Removes backside-cooling helium, one of a fab's largest helium uses, from etch, implant and CVD tools; zero per-wafer helium on those steps.

title: Po wordlines drawn in pencil: intercalated graphene buried wordlines
idea: Po: 'wordlines are drawn with a pencil.' Extracted: form buried wordlines from multilayer graphene precipitated at <500 C from a sacrificial nickel liner, then intercalate with FeCl3 or bromine to drop sheet resistance; graphene's resistivity does not rise at sub-10 nm widths the way tungsten's does from surface scattering.
why: Tungsten chokepoint (China ~80%) and WF6 fluorine chemistry removed from wordlines; at ~10 nm widths intercalated graphene could match or beat tungsten's effective resistivity, keeping wordline RC flat as cells shrink.

title: Po capacitor made of white paint: rutile TiO2 on MoO2 electrodes
idea: Po: 'the capacitor dielectric is the white pigment in house paint.' Extracted: grow rutile-phase TiO2 (k ~80-110) at low temperature by templating it on a rutile MoO2 bottom electrode, which is lattice-matched like RuO2 but made from U.S.-mined molybdenum, and Al-dope it to suppress leakage, replacing ZrO2/HfO2 stacks and ruthenium.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1 needs k ~70): k ~90 gives ~1.5-2x Cs at the same aspect ratio, or lets the AR fall from ~70 to ~40; titanium and molybdenum are abundant and U.S.-sourced (Climax, CO), removing hafnium and platinum-group dependence.

title: Po the fab never etches: bottom-up area-selective capacitor growth
idea: Po: 'the fab is forbidden to etch.' Extracted: grow capacitor pillars bottom-up by area-selective deposition, with inhibitor monolayers blocking growth on the oxide field while TiN or Mo grows only on exposed storage-node plugs, re-dosing the inhibitor every few nanometers to reach AR 60+. This removes the high-aspect-ratio fluorocarbon mold etch.
why: PFAS and fluorinated-gas intensity (the high-AR mold etch is a major C4F6/C4F8/NF3 consumer, GWP >7000) and etch-tool capex; also eliminates mold-collapse yield loss.

title: Po photoresist from shrimp shells: water-developed chitosan resist
idea: Po: 'photoresist is made from seafood waste.' Extracted: use a chemically modified chitosan or cellulose resist with non-fluorinated photo-crosslinkers that develops in plain water, applied to the non-critical DRAM layers (implants, pads, periphery), which are the majority of mask steps.
why: PFAS (fluorinated PAGs and surfactants facing EU restriction) and TMAH developer removed from most litho steps; renewable feedstock; lighter wastewater load.

title: Po the fab drinks no water: supercritical CO2 clean and dry
idea: Po: 'the fab is built in a desert with no water.' Extracted: replace post-etch residue removal, rinse and spin-dry on most cleaning steps with supercritical CO2 plus alcohol and chelating co-solvents, recaptured and recompressed in a closed loop; the zero surface tension of scCO2 also stops tall capacitor pillars collapsing during drying.
why: Water intensity (large fabs draw millions of gallons per day; cleaning is the biggest use) cut by perhaps 30-50%, and the capillary-collapse limit on capacitor aspect ratio (fact 1) is lifted.

title: Po cleanroom the size of a wafer: sealed nitrogen tool tunnels
idea: Po: 'the cleanroom is no bigger than the wafer.' Extracted: drop ballroom ISO-class cleanrooms and connect tools with sealed, nitrogen-purged carrier tunnels and tool-mounted mini-environments, so only ~2% of the building volume is ultraclean and the rest uses ordinary industrial HVAC.
why: Energy and capital: cleanroom air handling is roughly 30-40% of fab electricity and the shell is a large share of the $15B+ capex; cutting ultraclean volume ~50x could halve facility energy and shrink building cost.

title: Po memory that forgets on purpose: refresh-free ephemeral pages
idea: Po: 'memory that forgets on purpose.' Extracted: the OS and compiler tag pages whose data will be overwritten or discarded within the retention window (AI activations, KV-cache chunks, network buffers) as ephemeral; the controller skips refresh on those rows and stores an expiry timestamp so a late read faults instead of returning corrupt data.
why: Refresh energy (~46 fJ/bit, 16-33% of idle power, 10-20% of bandwidth at 32-64 Gb): on AI servers where much of DRAM holds short-lived tensors, refresh energy and bandwidth loss on those rows go to zero.

title: Po old DRAM is an ore body: urban-mined DIMM reclamation lines
idea: Po: 'the richest DRAM mine is a landfill.' Extracted: build automated lines that strip DRAM packages from DIMMs in decommissioned servers, retest each package at speed and temperature, re-bin, and re-mount them on CXL memory-expander cards whose controller maps out weak rows.
why: Effective supply: servers retire on 4-6-year cycles with healthy DRAM; reclaimed bits add supply with zero wafer starts, helium, quartz or EUV.

title: Po broken chips are the product: bank-salvage CXL memory
idea: Po: 'sell only the broken chips.' Extracted: dies that fail final test because of one or two dead banks or a slow mat, scrapped or downgraded today, are packaged with a small CXL controller that keeps a per-die bank map and presents a contiguous address space, priced per good GB.
why: Yield and resource intensity: recovers several percent of wafer output whose wafer, helium, crucible and EUV cost is already sunk; strongest for HBM-class dies with 20-30% lower yield.

title: Po wafers give birth: porous-silicon reusable parent wafer
idea: Po: 'a wafer is a mother that gives birth to daughters.' Extracted: anodize a double-porosity layer on a parent wafer, grow a 20-50 um device-quality epitaxial film on it, build the DRAM, bond to a carrier and split at the weak porous layer; re-polish and reuse the parent 10-20 times.
why: Crucible, polysilicon and ingot energy per DRAM wafer cut ~10x; the thin film also eases thermal management and die stacking.

title: Po DRAM on dirty silicon: metallurgical substrate plus thick epi
idea: Po: 'DRAM is built on dirty silicon.' Extracted: use cheap upgraded-metallurgical-grade (~5N) cast silicon as a mechanical substrate, add a heavily doped gettering and diffusion-barrier buried layer, then grow a thick epitaxial device layer from electronic-grade trichlorosilane, so only the top ~10 um needs 11N purity.
why: Electronic-grade polysilicon (Siemens process ~50-100 kWh/kg, few suppliers) and high-purity quartz crucibles largely bypassed; substrate cost and energy cut several-fold.

title: Po hafnium falls out of reactors: naval-zirconium hafnium chain
idea: Po: 'hafnium is nuclear waste.' Extracted: hafnium is separated only when nuclear-grade zirconium is made, so contract U.S. nuclear zirconium producers to convert their hafnium byproduct directly into HfCl4 and amide precursors at home, and qualify capacitor stacks that accept mixed Hf/Zr feed (HZO-like) so unseparated, cheaper feedstock works.
why: Hafnium and precursor import dependence: a captive U.S. chain from existing nuclear Zr plants; accepting mixed Hf/Zr skips the costly separation step for dielectric use.

title: Po the capacitor is a battery: solid-electrolyte double-layer storage
idea: Po: 'the DRAM capacitor is a tiny battery.' Extracted: replace the high-k film with a few-nm solid proton conductor (e.g. hydrated phosphosilicate glass) between ion-blocking electrodes, storing charge in an electric double layer of ~10-20 uF/cm2; the ion conductor is engineered so the double layer forms in under 10 ns.
why: Capacitor charge wall: ~1.5-3x capacitance per area over ZrO2-based stacks without hafnium, letting the capacitor be much shorter; speed and leakage are the open questions.

title: Po the crystal draws the pattern: facet-defined sub-litho fins
idea: Po: 'the crystal is the lithographer.' Extracted: on (110) silicon, TMAH wet etch stops on vertical {111} planes, so a coarse 40 nm DUV pattern yields atomically flat vertical walls; self-limiting oxidation then thins fins to 8-10 nm, giving access-transistor fins and buried-wordline trenches without EUV.
why: EUV single-supplier chokepoint (5-7 EUV layers): replaces 2-3 EUV layers with DUV plus wet chemistry, and the wet etch avoids fluorinated plasma gases.

title: Po chips stamped like coins: nanoimprint for cell-array layers
idea: Po: 'memory is minted like coins.' Extracted: use step-and-repeat nanoimprint with replica templates for the highly regular cell-array layers (bitlines, storage-node contacts) and keep DUV for periphery; the imprint tool uses a small fraction of an EUV scanner's power and no tin or hydrogen plasma.
why: EUV capital (~$200M+ per scanner) and energy (~1 MW each) on array layers; template defectivity is the gate.

title: Po every gas well is a helium well: fab-anchored membrane extraction
idea: Po: 'every gas well near the fab is a helium mine.' Extracted: install modular hollow-fiber membrane plus PSA skids on U.S. pipeline gas streams with only 0.1-0.5% helium, normally uneconomic, co-located near fabs in Arizona, Texas and New York, and justify them with fab waste heat and long-term offtake contracts.
why: Helium supply security: many low-helium streams are vented or ignored; fab-anchored micro-extraction could cover a fab's net make-up need from domestic gas.

title: Po the fab has no drain: zero-liquid-discharge with fluoride mining
idea: Po: 'the fab has no drain pipe.' Extracted: segregate wastewater by chemistry, reclaim >90% to UPW feed with RO and electrodeionization, crystallize the brine, and precipitate fluoride as acid-grade CaF2 (a fluorspar substitute) and ammonia as fertilizer for sale.
why: Water intensity (net intake falls ~5-10x) and fluorspar (China-dominated) partly offset by recovered fluoride; makes fabs viable in water-stressed U.S. states.

title: Po dies stacked without touching: inductive-coupled TSV-free HBM
idea: Po: 'stacked dies that never touch.' Extracted: replace thousands of copper TSVs with on-die spiral-coil inductive transceivers that couple data through 20-50 um thinned dies, and bring power in through edge-plated pads, so DRAM dies need no TSV keep-out zones and no via-reveal process.
why: HBM TSV tax (~3x wafer area per bit vs DDR5, yield down 20-30%): recovers most TSV area plus copper fill and reveal steps; coil arrays sit in top metal over the array.

title: Po one lightbulb lights the whole fab: shared FEL EUV source
idea: Po: 'one lightbulb lights every scanner in the fab.' Extracted: drive 10-20 scanners from a single energy-recovery-linac free-electron laser at 13.5 nm, distributed by grazing-incidence beamlines, replacing per-scanner tin-droplet laser-produced-plasma sources.
why: EUV energy (~1 MW per LPP scanner) and tin/hydrogen consumption: several-fold lower wall-plug energy per exposed wafer and higher available dose, which permits lower-defect resists.

title: Po the chip is the whole wafer: 200 mm wafer-scale memory slab
idea: Po: 'one chip per wafer.' Extracted: on a fully depreciated 200 mm, 180 nm fab, pattern one wafer-scale DRAM with 4-8% redundant mats and 1990s laser-fuse rerouting, stitch a global bus with the stepper, and mount the slab with edge connectors; no dicing, bumping or packaging.
why: Capital intensity and U.S. manufacturability: depreciation (~55% of wafer cost) goes to ~0; ~6 GB per slab (8F2 cell ~0.26 um2, ~50% array efficiency) of cheap, domestic capacity-tier memory with packaging and test cost per bit far lower.

title: Po chips talk through their sides: edge-metallized DRAM die cube
idea: Po: 'dies speak through their edges, not their faces.' Extracted: lap 180 nm DRAM dies to ~100 um, laminate 32-64 of them with adhesive, polish one face of the stack, and sputter and photo-pattern sidewall bus lines that join edge-routed pads (the 1990s Irvine Sensors memory-cube approach).
why: HBM TSV tax and density: 32-64x bits per footprint with no TSVs, no hybrid bonding and no copper via fill, all on U.S. 200 mm-era tools.

title: Po light digs the holes: electrochemical macroporous silicon trench capacitors
idea: Po: 'let light dig the holes.' Extracted: seed pits with a KrF stepper, then anodize n-type silicon in HF under backside illumination so pores grow straight to aspect ratios of 100-250 with no plasma; line them with thermal oxide/nitride and fill with doped poly to form trench storage capacitors.
why: Capacitor charge wall (AR ~115 needed) reached without plasma etch or high-k: at ~0.4 um pore pitch and AR ~200, Cs of 30-60 fF with ONO, which relaxes refresh; no Hf, Zr, W or fluorocarbon gas.

title: Po the cell latches like a light switch: implanted vertical thyristor
idea: Po: 'memory that holds itself like a light switch.' Extracted: build a p-n-p-n thyristor vertically in bulk silicon with stacked high-energy implants under a 180 nm pillar, gated by one wordline; the cell latches on or off with no capacitor or high-k and holds data with a tiny standby bias instead of refresh.
why: Removes capacitor materials (Hf, Zr, TiN) and the charge wall; a ~4F2 vertical cell lets a 180 nm line reach useful density, with refresh replaced by low hold current.

title: Po holes arrange themselves: anodic-alumina template with anodized-titanium dielectric
idea: Po: 'holes that arrange themselves.' Extracted: anodize a sputtered aluminum film so it self-organizes into a hexagonal array of 30-60 nm pores microns deep, sputter or CVD titanium into the pores and anodize it into a conformal TiO2 dielectric; the self-ordered pores give each 180 nm cell many sub-litho capacitor tubes.
why: Charge wall and litho-bound scaling: ~10-20x capacitor area per cell footprint without EUV, ALD or hafnium; aluminum and titanium are abundant and U.S.-produced.

title: Po memory from four common elements: HSG polysilicon ONO capacitor
idea: Po: 'the cell contains only silicon, oxygen, nitrogen and phosphorus.' Extracted: revive the late-1990s stacked capacitor with hemispherical-grain rugged polysilicon electrodes (2-2.5x area), a thin nitrided oxide-nitride dielectric and doped-poly plugs, removing TiN, Ru, Zr, Hf and W from the cell.
why: Scarce-resource intensity: zero chokepoint metals in the array, fully U.S.-manufacturable on 200 mm tools; density is modest but material supply risk falls to ~0.

title: Po tungsten never existed: high-pressure aluminum force-fill plugs
idea: Po: 'tungsten was never discovered.' Extracted: fill all contacts and vias with PVD aluminum forced into the holes at ~700 atm and ~400 C (the mid-1990s force-fill method) over a thin Ti wetting layer, replacing CVD tungsten plugs and the WF6 precursor.
why: Tungsten chokepoint (China ~80%) and fluorine chemistry removed from interconnect; aluminum is abundant and U.S.-smelted, with lower via resistance than tungsten.

title: Po the array is a hologram: interference-lithography cell arrays
idea: Po: 'the memory array is a hologram.' Extracted: expose the periodic array layers (active lines, wordlines, bitlines) by two- and four-beam interference of a 1990s frequency-quadrupled 266 nm laser, printing ~150 nm-pitch gratings over a whole 200 mm wafer at once; a KrF stepper then trims at mat edges and patterns the periphery.
why: Litho capital and masks: array layers need no reticle and no scanner time, at roughly 2x finer pitch than the stepper alone, with U.S.-buildable optics.

title: Po wafers have no back: double-sided arrays on one wafer
idea: Po: 'the wafer has no back side.' Extracted: double-side-polish 200 mm wafers, build transistors and capacitors on the front, flip and build a second array on the back with a low-temperature capacitor module last, and connect the faces at die edges for power and I/O.
why: Silicon, crucible quartz and wafer starts per bit halved: one wafer carries two arrays at 180 nm, lowering substrate and some tool costs per bit.

title: Po memory never forgets because it is cold: 77 K planar cells
idea: Po: 'memory that never forgets.' Extracted: run 180 nm-built DRAM in liquid nitrogen, where junction and subthreshold leakage fall by many orders of magnitude, so a simple planar MOS capacitor of 3-5 fF holds data for hours and refresh nearly vanishes; LN2 comes from air, not helium.
why: Lets cheap planar 180 nm cells (no high-AR etch, no high-k) work; refresh energy ~0 and transistors get faster; the price is ~10 W of wall power per W removed at 77 K, best in already-cooled racks.

title: Po memory made of sandpaper: silicon-carbide refresh-free DRAM
idea: Po: 'memory made of sandpaper.' Extracted: build 1T1C cells in 4H silicon carbide (carborundum) on 150 mm SiC lines with >=0.5 um tools; the 3.2 eV bandgap cuts thermal generation leakage so cells hold charge for hours to years at room temperature, as 1990s SiC DRAM experiments showed.
why: Refresh eliminated (fact 3) and U.S. manufacturability (SiC fabs in NC and NY); density is low but energy per bit for refresh-free working memory drops sharply.

title: Po the test wafer is the product: reclaimed monitor-wafer substrates
idea: Po: 'the test wafer is the product.' Extracted: route the large stream of 200 mm monitor and dummy wafers used for tool qualification through CMP reclaim plus a thin epitaxial refresh layer, and run them as product substrates for 180 nm memory instead of virgin prime wafers.
why: Virgin polysilicon, crucible quartz and wafer energy per bit cut sharply for legacy memory; reclaim wafers cost roughly a third to a half of prime.

title: Po the crucible is brewed in a test tube: sol-gel silica liners
idea: Po: 'the crucible is brewed in a test tube.' Extracted: for 150-200 mm pullers, whose crucibles are small, cast the melt-contact liner from synthetic silica made by sol-gel hydrolysis of silicon alkoxides (or flame hydrolysis of SiCl4) and sinter it onto a lower-grade quartz back wall, ending reliance on Spruce Pine natural quartz.
why: Breaks the >80% high-purity-quartz crucible chokepoint for 200 mm legacy-memory wafers on 1990s pullers; synthetic silica is purer than natural quartz.

title: Po the fab never heard of helium: batch-tool gas-free flow
idea: Po: 'the fab has never heard of helium.' Extracted: build the 180 nm DRAM flow around batch vertical furnaces (LPCVD poly, nitride, oxide), wet etches and low-power batch plasma tools whose wafers sit on boats or mechanical clamps needing no backside gas; use hydrogen or argon for any leak checks and purges.
why: Helium (Qatar supply offline): zero helium in the bill of materials; batch tools also cost far less per wafer-pass.

title: Po one cell holds four voltages: multi-level big-capacitor cells
idea: Po: 'each cell remembers a number, not a bit.' Extracted: use the large storage capacitance practical at 180 nm (30+ fF with trench or HSG capacitors) to store four charge levels (2 bits per cell), read with reference-ladder sense amplifiers and a two-step compare; refresh restores the levels.
why: Density: doubles bits per area on old tools, closing part of the 180 nm vs 12 nm gap on a depreciated domestic line, at a cost of roughly 2x row access time.

title: Po the chip is mostly air: air-gap bitlines shrink capacitors
idea: Po: 'the chip is mostly air.' Extracted: after patterning bitlines, cap them with non-conformal PECVD oxide that pinches off above the spaces, leaving air (k ~1) between neighbors; bitline capacitance falls ~40%, so the same sense signal needs ~40% less storage capacitance.
why: Capacitor charge wall: signal depends on Cs/Cb, so lower Cb allows shorter, cheaper capacitors and cuts bitline CV2 energy ~30-40%.

title: Po transistors from solder metals: indium-gallium-free zinc-tin-oxide gain cells
idea: Po: 'the transistor is made from melted solder.' Extracted: RF-sputter amorphous zinc-tin oxide channels for 2T gain cells patterned with i-line/KrF tools at <=350 C, replacing IGZO's indium and gallium (gallium refining ~98% Chinese) with abundant zinc and tin while keeping very low off-current.
why: Scarce-resource intensity for oxide-semiconductor memory; low-temperature gain-cell layers can be stacked over 180 nm CMOS to add density without new litho.

title: Po fab tools are open-source: cloned 1990s equipment designs
idea: Po: 'semiconductor tools are open-source like Linux.' Extracted: fund a public library of reverse-engineered, patent-expired 1990s tool designs (i-line/KrF steppers, LPCVD furnaces, RIE, implanters) and certify U.S. machine shops to build them, so new 200 mm memory lines need not wait on a shrinking used-tool market.
why: Capital intensity and U.S. manufacturability: domestic clones could cut legacy-line capex 3-5x and remove tool scarcity as the limit on new 200 mm capacity.

title: Po no fab owns a whole chip: relay-fab consortium of 200mm sites
idea: Po: 'no fab makes a whole chip.' Extracted: split the 180 nm DRAM flow into modules (front-end transistors, capacitor module, metallization, test) assigned to under-used U.S. 200 mm analog and MEMS fabs, moving wafers between them in sealed carriers under a shared copy-exact spec and a pooled tooling fund.
why: U.S. manufacturability and capital: uses existing idle capacity instead of a $15B greenfield fab, with time to first supply measured in months.

title: Po oxide is only grown, never etched: fluorine-free LOCOS flow
idea: Po: 'oxide may only be grown, never etched.' Extracted: define isolation and contact windows by local oxidation through nitride masks (LOCOS and poly-buffered LOCOS), etch silicon, poly and aluminum only with chlorine and bromine plasmas, strip nitride in hot phosphoric acid, and drop fluorocarbon oxide etches entirely.
why: PFAS and fluorinated greenhouse gases (CF4, C2F6, NF3; GWP 6,500-17,000) cut to near zero in a memory flow that 1990s tools support natively.

title: Po energy is borrowed, never spent: resonant inductor wordline drivers
idea: Po: 'the memory borrows energy and gives it back.' Extracted: drive wordlines and bitline precharge from resonant LC tanks built with thick top-metal on-die inductors (easy in 180 nm aluminum processes), ramping lines slowly and returning their charge to the tank instead of dumping it to ground.
why: Voltage floor (CV2 stuck at ~1 V array and ~3 V wordline): 50-70% energy recovery on wordline and bitline swings; 180 nm thick-oxide devices handle the swings natively.

title: Po the transistor stands up: vertical surrounding-gate 4F2 cells
idea: Po: 'the transistor stands on its head.' Extracted: etch silicon pillars with a KrF stepper, wrap each in a gate by conformal LPCVD poly and spacer etch (Toshiba's 1988 surrounding-gate transistor), with buried diffused bitlines below and the capacitor on top, giving a 4F2 cell.
why: Density at old pitch: 4F2 vs 8F2 halves cell area, so a 180 nm U.S. line gets ~2x bits per wafer without any litho upgrade.

title: Po memory that never shrinks: perpetual-node legacy DRAM franchise
idea: Po: 'memory that never shrinks.' Extracted: freeze a copy-exact 180-150 nm DRAM process for 20+ years and sell long-life legacy parts (SDR to DDR3, small densities, industrial, auto and defense) under take-or-pay supply contracts, so those markets stop consuming leading-edge wafers and end-of-life buys.
why: Effective supply: legacy-DRAM end-of-life notices fed the 2025-26 price spikes; a perpetual U.S. node moves those bits off leading-edge capacity with no mask or node R&D churn and ~0 depreciation after year 5.
